title: Wickliffe as bandleader and the Windsor Theater job
summary: Wickliffe was a good talker who got good men and good pay, including a Windsor Theater job paying $45 a week.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: He's over 15. They tell me that Wickliffe was a very progressive sort of fellow. Now, as a drummer, was he just smart enough to get the right men?

Smart enough to get the right men, yeah. He always had a good band. And he was a good talker and getting jobs. And when he got a good job, he could always come around and say, I got a good job. He's paying so much money a week. And I want a good trumpet player and something like that. He would get the men. Because I know one time we played a theater, the Windsor Theater on Clark Street near the vision, I imagine it was. It was the first time they ever had a jazz band in that theater. And the man said, you run the people out. And Wickliffe talked to him and used such persuasion language as the man hired us and paid us, I think, an enormous sum. I think the units gave us around $25 a week and we got $45. The side man got $45, which was a big sum in the 1920 or 21, whatever it was. And we played when the comedy came on. Then we played.
We were in the box. Oh. In the box. They put us in the box. And if I'm not mistaken, I think Bob Schauffner was playing trumpet then. I think he came up from St. Louis.
Did you play every show? Or just even?

Well, we played every evening. We played every show and we played only on the comedies. I think they had a couple of comedies we played about a half hour. And then we were off to pictures about an hour. We were off an hour. It was a piece of a job.
